chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gestures (with his head) in the obligatory and voluntary prayers if he cannot find something to prostrate upon and has no place to prostrate in. He said: 'If it is so, then he should gesture throughout the entire prayer.'

key_terms.يُومِئُ: He gestures (with the head as a substitute for prostration)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they cannot find a place or object to prostrate on during prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the concession for one lacking a proper surface for forehead contact, ruling that head nodding (*i'nam*) suffices for the entire prayer duration. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of *rukū'* and *sujūd* being primarily acts of the heart and body, where physical impediments allow for proportional gesturing rather than invalidating the prayer. It underscores the flexibility in ritual purity and posture, ensuring the validity of both *fard* and *nafl* prayers under duress.
